composing_text: 44th (Lowland) Infantry Brigade; 46th (Highland) Infantry Brigade; 227th (Highland) Infantry Brigade
notes: Landed about 14 June (Wikipedia list; landing beach shown uncertain).

current_activity: leading Epsom and fighting at Cheux
notes: Led Epsom; by end of 26 June overran most of the German outpost line; fighting at Cheux/Sainte-Manvieu against 12th SS and 21st Panzer.

Secured Grainville-sur-Odon by 13:00 28 June after street fighting; Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders took the bridge and village of Gavrus south of the Odon; Kampfgruppe Weidinger attacks on Grainville and Mondrainville held. Battle group Frey (1st SS) took Mouen.

current_activity: Preliminary attacks: takes Bougy and Gavrus on the Evrecy road; Esquay is entered but not held
notes: Event date: 15-17 July 1944 (night of the 15th to the 17th) (Ellis, vol. I, p. 334). Event definition: In the fighting from the night of 15 July to the opening of Goodwood the division, in XII Corps, takes Bougy and Gavrus; it enters Esquay but cannot hold it, and after repeated attacks and counter-attacks Esquay stays in German hands. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 334: "In XII Corps area on the left, Bougy and Gavrus were taken by the 15th Division; Esquay was entered but could not be held". Location: Bougy, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Bougy; Gavrus lies close by and the dates are those of the three-day fight, not one day. Location support: Ellis names Bougy and Gavrus as taken by the division (p. 334).

current_activity: Bluecoat: advances from the Caumont ridge at about 07:00 with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade towards Point 309
notes: Event date: 30 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 388, 390, 391). Event definition: The division, with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade in support and the 11th Armoured Division on its right, begins its advance a few minutes before 07:00 from the Caumont ridge; the first objectives (two villages near Caumont, then les Loges and Point 226) are taken by about 10:00 and Point 309 is the objective of the day; mines put seven Churchills and two flail tanks out of action (pp. 388 and 390). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 388: "Point 309. It is marked by a quarry show- ing just below the summit and was the first day's objective of VIII Corps' 15th Division"; pp. 390-391: "with the 6th Guards Tank Brigade in support, and the 11th Armoured Division on their right began their advance a few minutes before seven". Location: Caumont-l'Eventé (existing place PL0071), the start area with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Caumont, from which the advance started; Point 309 itself is not located. Location support: Ellis names the Caumont ridge as the start and Point 309 as the objective, which is not in the gazetteers used (pp. 388 and 390).

current_activity: Crosses the Seine in stormboats and Dukws near St. Pierre-du-Vauvray; the bridgeheads join by 11:00 on 28 August
notes: Event date: 27 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 455, 467). Event definition: The division assaults across the Seine on 27 August: one brigade crosses in stormboats, followed by Dukws, near St. Pierre-du-Vauvray, about two miles from Louviers, losing three boats and suffering heavy casualties, and a second crosses near Portejoie; by 11:00 on 28 August the two bridgeheads are joined and the third brigade crosses at Muids (p. 467). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 455: "The commander of the 15th Division planned to assault on the 27th"; p. 467: "One brigade of the 15th (Scottish) Division had crossed in stormboats followed by Dukws near St. Pierre du Vauvray, about two miles from Louviers (losing three boats to machine-gun fire, with heavy casualties)". Location: Saint-Pierre-du-Vauvray, Eure (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis names St. Pierre du Vauvray (p. 467).

current_activity: Veritable: the 46th Brigade clears Frasselt by dark and the 227th Brigade captures Kranenburg
notes: Event date: 8 February 1945 (by dark) (Ellis, vol. II, p. 259). Event definition: On 8 February the division is to seize the key ground about Cleve after breaching the Siegfried defences; it leads with two brigades, the 46th on the right and the 227th on the left, who have more trouble with mines and mud than with the enemy; with close support from artillery and flame-throwers the 46th Brigade clears the long straggling village of Frasselt by dark and the 227th Brigade captures Kranenburg; the 44th Brigade, which is to force the Siegfried line, is delayed on a rough track and begins only at four in the morning (p. 259). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 259: "The 15th Divisional Group was faced with the task of seizing the key ground about Cleve, first breaching the Siegfried defences on the way"; "the 46th Brigade had cleared the long straggling village of Frasselt by dark and the 227th Brigade captured Kranenburg". Location: Kranenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the village of Kranenburg; the division headquarters is not named and Frasselt, also cleared, lies a few kilometres to the south-east. Location support: Ellis names Kranenburg as the village the 227th Brigade captured (p. 259).

current_activity: Veritable: the 44th Brigade breaches the Siegfried defences and reaches the Bresserberg ridge by dark, by Cleve
notes: Event date: 9 February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 262). Event definition: On 9 February the day's most important advances are made by the 44th Brigade, supported by tanks of the 6th Guards Armoured Brigade and equipments of the 79th Armoured Division: it begins before dawn against the Siegfried defences just north-east of Frasselt, has three crossings of the anti-tank ditch in use by nine o'clock, collects about 400 prisoners, enters Nutterden, and as darkness falls gains a sound footing on the Bresserberg ridge, just off the western outskirts of Cleve and barely a mile from Materborn village; troops of the German 7th Parachute Division fail to regain the ridge in the evening, but the road between Cleve and Materborn is still blocked (p. 262). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 262: "The day's most important advances were made by the 44th Brigade"; "The advance had begun before dawn against the Siegfried defences just north-east of Frasselt"; "gained a sound footing on the Bresserberg ridge, just off the western outskirts of Cleve and barely a mile from Materborn village". Location: Cleve, North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0578), the town beside the Bresserberg ridge with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Cleve, about two kilometres east of the Bresserberg ridge; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis puts the Bresserberg ridge just off the western outskirts of Cleve (p. 262).

current_activity: Veritable: fights its way into Cleve against determined opposition; the town is cleared and handed over next day
notes: Event date: 11 February 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 264). Event definition: On 11 February the division fights its way into Cleve against determined opposition and enables the 43rd Division's brigade to disengage, though not before that brigade has broken up an early morning attack by paratroops and taken 180 of them prisoner; hardly a house is standing in Cleve and next day the town is finally cleared and handed over to the 3rd Canadian Division; the 46th Brigade then sets out for Calcar with a mobile column (p. 264). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 264: "On the 11th the 15th Division had fought their way into Cleve against determined opposition"; "next day the town was finally cleared and handed over to the 3rd Canadian Division". Location: Cleve, North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0578) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Cleve; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Cleve as the town fought into (p. 264).

current_activity: Veritable: takes over the attack at the escarpment; forces the inner anti-tank ditch; fighting in Goch by midnight
notes: Event date: 18 February 1945, to midnight (Ellis, vol. II, p. 267). Event definition: After the 43rd Division has secured the escarpment north-east of Goch on the 17th and its engineers have opened seven crossings over the outer anti-tank ditch, the 15th Division's leading brigade takes up the attack on the morning of 18 February; greatly helped by the special equipments of the 79th Armoured Division the Scots force an inner anti-tank ditch and by midnight are fighting in the environs of Goch, as are troops of the 53rd Division to their right and a brigade of the 51st on the far side of the Niers; the garrison commander surrenders the next day, but confused fighting in the rubble goes on for another 48 hours (p. 267). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 267: "next morning the 15th Division's leading brigade took up the attack"; "by midnight were fighting in the environs of Goch". Location: Goch, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Goch; the division fought on the north side, in the environs, and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Goch as the town the division fought in (p. 267).
